title: IP Address
body:
The numeric address a machine is reachable at on a network. [[DNS]] exists to turn hostnames into these.

**IPv4** is 32 bits, written as four dotted octets (`142.250.190.78`), giving about 4.3 billion possible addresses — a pool that has been globally exhausted for years. **IPv6** is 128 bits (`2001:0db8:85a3::8a2e:0370:7334`) and is functionally unlimited; it exists specifically to solve that exhaustion.

Addresses split into two kinds. A **private IP** (`192.168.x.x`, `10.x.x.x`) is assigned by your own router and is meaningful only inside your local network — millions of homes are simultaneously using `192.168.1.1`. A **public IP** is the single address your household presents to the internet, and the translation between the two is done by your router via [[NAT]], which keeps a table so replies get routed back to the right device.
